cards.text: We're up north in Israel now. In the twenty-third year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu becomes king of Israel, and he reigns in Samaria seventeen years. Stay close, friend, because this chapter is a whole parade of kings with names that sound alike.

cards.question: True or false: King Jehoahaz turns away from the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat, an earlier king, had caused Israel to commit.

cards.text: So the anger of the LORD burns against Israel. Over and over, He hands them over to Hazael king of Aram, and then to his son Ben-hadad.

cards.question: Aram keeps crushing Israel. What does King Jehoahaz do?

answers.text: He seeks the favor of the LORD
He sends gold to King Hazael
He asks Egypt to send help

cards.question: The LORD listens to King Jehoahaz. Why does the text say He listens?

answers.text: He saw how Aram oppressed Israel

cards.question: The LORD answers. He gives Israel a ___, and they escape the power of the Arameans.

cards.text: Free from Aram, the people of Israel live in their own homes again, the way they did before. I bet it felt like my first day out of the junk drawer: ROOM. TO. STRETCH.

cards.question: True or false: Once they're rescued, Israel finally turns away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam.

cards.text: Nope, they keep walking in those same sins, and the Asherah pole even stays standing right there in Samaria. That's me getting pulled out of the junk drawer and asking, "Wait, can I go back in for a nap?"
Here's how bad things got for Jehoahaz. The king of Aram destroyed his army and made them like the dust at threshing.

cards.question: True or false: Aram leaves King Jehoahaz with only ten chariots.

cards.text: TEN chariots, fifty horsemen and ten thousand foot soldiers, and that's the WHOLE army. Then Jehoahaz rests with his fathers and is buried in Samaria, and the rest of his story is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

cards.question: King Jehoahaz has died. Who reigns in his place?

cards.text: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz becomes king of Israel in Samaria, and he reigns sixteen years. Joash in Judah, Jehoash in Israel, same time, almost the same name: that's two guys named Mike in one group chat, and NOBODY knows who's replying.

cards.question: New king, new start? What does King Jehoash do in the sight of the LORD?

answers.text: Evil by walking in Jeroboam's sins
Right by tearing down the Asherah pole
Right by listening to the prophets

cards.text: The rest of his story, including his war against Amaziah king of Judah, is written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. Then Jehoash rests with his fathers and is buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

cards.question: King Jehoash is gone. Who takes the throne after him?

cards.text: Now the story steps back into the days of King Jehoash. Elisha, the prophet, has fallen sick with the illness he will die from, and Jehoash comes down to see him.

cards.question: King Jehoash stands beside the dying prophet Elisha. What does the king do?

answers.text: He asks Elisha to anoint him
He sits beside Elisha in silence

cards.text: He cries, "My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!" Then Elisha, sick in bed, tells the king to take a bow and some arrows, and the king does it.

cards.question: True or false: Elisha tells King Jehoash to put his hand on the bow, and then Elisha puts his own hands on the king's hands.

cards.text: Elisha tells him to open the east window. Then Elisha says, "Shoot!" and the king shoots.

cards.question: King Jehoash's arrow flies out the east window. What does Elisha say that arrow is?

answers.text: The LORD's arrow of victory over Aram
A sign that Elisha will be healed
A warning to the king of Judah

cards.text: Then Elisha says, "Take the arrows!" The king takes them, and Elisha says, "Strike the ground!"

cards.question: King Jehoash takes the arrows and strikes the ground ___ times, and then he stops.
True or false: Elisha, the man of God, is pleased with how many times King Jehoash struck the ground.

cards.text: Elisha is angry and tells him, "You should have struck the ground five or six times." Three and done, friend? That's me stamping three cookies, untying my apron and calling it a batch.

cards.question: King Jehoash stopped at three. Now what does Elisha say the king will do to Aram?

answers.text: Strike down Aram only three times

cards.text: Then Elisha dies and is buried. Raiders from Moab used to come into the land every spring, and once, while some Israelites are burying a man, they suddenly see a band of raiders.

cards.question: Raiders are coming, and these Israelites still have a body to bury. What do they do with it?
True or false: When the man's body touches the bones of Elisha, the man comes back to life.

cards.text: As soon as his body touches Elisha's bones, the man is revived and stands up on his feet. WHAT?! This man went into that tomb lying down and ended up STANDING UP!
All through the reign of Jehoahaz, Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel. But the LORD is gracious to Israel, has compassion on them and turns toward them.

cards.question: Israel keeps walking in sin, yet the LORD turns toward them. Why does the text say He does it?

answers.text: His covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob
Israel finally tore down its idols

cards.text: When Hazael king of Aram dies, his son Ben-hadad reigns in his place. Now King Jehoash gets his shot at Ben-hadad.

cards.question: Think back to those arrows on the ground. How many times does King Jehoash defeat Ben-hadad?

cards.text: With those wins, Jehoash takes back the cities Hazael had taken in battle from his father Jehoahaz. Three strikes on the ground, three wins, just like Elisha said, and I bet that king wished he'd kept swinging those arrows.

findings.problem: This story card carries three beats: what is left of Jehoahaz's army (v7), the rest of his acts being written in the Chronicles (v8), and his death and burial in Samaria (v9).

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: One wrong answer is "Right by listening to the prophets." Later in the passage Jehoash does listen to Elisha and follows each of his instructions (2 Kings 13:15-18). A baker could argue that this answer is partly true.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Jeroboam," is a new person (Jehoash's son, Jeroboam II). No card ever says who he is. The only Jeroboam the baker has met is "Jeroboam son of Nebat, an earlier king" (card 2). The baker can't tell the two apart, so the pick is confusing or comes down to luck, and nothing afterward clears it up.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: No card tells the rest of Elisha's declaration in v17: "you shall strike the Arameans in Aphek until you have put an end to them." Card 10 also drops the matching line in v19: "Then you would have struck down Aram until you had put an end to it." Without these lines the baker misses the point of the arrows, which is the contrast between putting an end to Aram and striking it only three times.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card carries three beats: Elisha dies and is buried, Moabite raiders used to come every spring, and Israelites burying a man spot a band of raiders. Elisha's death is a major moment and is folded in with the others. The stop is already at 20 cards, so splitting this card means trimming somewhere else, for example merging cards 14 and 15.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: No card tells the end of v23: "And to this day, the LORD has been unwilling to destroy them or cast them from His presence." This is a key statement of the LORD's mercy in the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question opens with "Israel keeps walking in sin," which rules out the wrong answer "Israel finally tore down its idols."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer, "His covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob," is noticeably longer than the two wrong answers and sounds more like the Bible, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
